Waste Crisis: Local, Small, and Thoughtful Solutions
This conversation is for those who want to do something effective to improve Iran's situation. Waste management in Iran is not in good shape. The northern provinces of Gilan and Mazandaran are in far worse condition, and the mountains of waste show that the crisis has become chronic. Waste causes pollution of water, soil, and air, and has adverse effects on human health.

Watch the conversation: https://youtu.be/R7CB2RPvoWc

Narges Azari has researched and worked on waste management for ten years, examined waste management policy-making, and ultimately established a think tank for thinking and acting on waste management. In this conversation, she recounts the problems of waste management, policy shortcomings, stories of failures, and instances of successes in this field.

entry.title: [fazelimohammadir] Give the gasoline to the people: fixing the imbalance with quota certificates.…
entry.summary:
Source: @fazelimohammadir

Give the gasoline to the people: fixing the imbalance with quota certificates. Sadegh Al-Hosseini argues that all the solutions proposed by the Ministry of Oil, the Plan and Budget Organization, and other solutions offered by others are inefficient and have more side effects compared to a plan based on giving an equal share of subsidized gasoline to all people. Watch the interview: https://youtu.be/4v6GxJolE9A. Al-Hosseini believes that by distributing an equal quota among all Iranians, based on a distribution of 90 million liters per day, and setting aside 30 million liters for working cars and motorcycles, the gasoline imbalance can be treated, and more importantly, an economic mechanism free from government intervention can be created to optimize equipment and energy consumers. In this detailed interview, he explains all aspects of his plan and finally addresses criticisms against the removal of the preferential exchange rate. This interview was recorded in response to Mohsen Yazdanpanah's critiques of the equal gasoline quota plan for everyone, which was previously published on IranTalk. entry.summary:

Solutions to the Iran-US conflict: from a national doctrine to redefining power. Sahand Iranmehr is an expert in international relations and foreign policy, although he is better known as a literary author. In this conversation, he examines the history of the Iran-US conflict from the Pahlavi era to the present day to reach the complexities of this relationship and show why this relationship can only be managed through a gradual process. Watch the conversation: https://youtu.be/G4p9D-CB28A. Sahand Iranmehr believes that the recent wars between the two countries have created grounds for different perceptions of the two countries' situations relative to each other, and despite all the mistrust, grounds have been created to move past tension and gradually move toward a state of conflict containment and competition management. He offers various solutions, including presenting a national doctrine to redefining power, as solutions for managing the Iran-US conflict.
